reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown read Jeremiah's denial as a Hebrew comparative meaning obedience mattered more than sacrifice, not that sacrifice was uncommanded.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen reads Jeremiah's denial at face value: sacrificial law was unknown to the wilderness generation, so it cannot be Mosaic.

quotes.text: Add your burnt-offerings to your sacrifices, and eat flesh! For I said nought unto your fathers, and commanded them nought, in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt-offerings or sacrifices.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), ch. on Jeremiah and the cultus, on Jeremiah 7:21-22.

sides.snippet: You shall make an altar of earth for me, and shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace-offerings, your sheep and your oxen.
sides.verseText: You shall make an altar of earth for me, and shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace-offerings, your sheep and your oxen. In every place where I record my name I will come to you and I will bless you.

sides.snippet: For I didn't speak to your fathers, nor command them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices:
